elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 14(a): "This Agreement is governed in all respects by the laws of the State of New York without giving effect to its conflict of laws principles." Only the jurisdiction word was swapped from Delaware to New York.

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 14(a): "Each Party hereby irrevocably submits for all disputes to the exclusive jurisdiction and venue of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York." The competing mandatory AAA arbitration sentence in Section 8 has been struck, so no alternate merits forum survives; the absence of a temporary-injunctive-relief carve-out does not defeat the element, which permits but does not require that customary exception.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause selects New York law, not Delaware, California, or England and Wales. This is a deliberate move to the preferred level, so the fallback checklist is simply not the level being satisfied.

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: Forum is the state and federal courts in New York County, New York ", i.e., neither Delaware/California courts nor the courts of London. Not applicable at the chosen preferred level.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: New York substantive law plus exclusive state and federal court jurisdiction in New York County, with the conflicting mandatory arbitration mechanic removed so the exclusive court forum is not internally contradicted.

Deviation classification is correct on the original text: Delaware law paired with New York venue matched neither level's law/forum pairing, and Section 8's mandatory AAA arbitration displaced any court forum entirely, a material failure of the fallback dispute-forum element.

Minimality holds. Only the jurisdiction word in the governing-law sentence, the venue words ("New York, New York" to "New York County, New York"), and the single arbitration sentence changed. Deleting the arbitration sentence is necessary, not cosmetic, because it otherwise contradicts the exclusive court jurisdiction the checklist requires. Retitling Section 8 from "Arbitration" to "Jury Trial Waiver" is a consequential conforming edit that avoids a heading with no corresponding operative text, not an added requirement.

Favourable and unrelated language survives: the jury-trial waiver, the one-year limitation on actions, and the conflict-of-laws exclusion are all retained verbatim. No new obligation, survival tail, procedure, or boilerplate was added, and no cross-reference is left dangling by the deletion.

Note for the record: no temporary-injunctive-relief carve-out was added. None is required, since an unqualified exclusive merits forum is at least as protective as the element's "subject only to" allowance; if the counterparty asks for interim relief flexibility, a carve-out limited strictly to temporary injunctive relief may be conceded without leaving the preferred position.
